reader.requirement: ORD-MIN compares its arguments by the 1985 simple-condition (relation) rules: numeric by algebraic value regardless of size/scale/sign, nonnumeric by the program collating sequence with the shorter operand space-extended on the right; alphabetic mixed with alphanumeric compares as nonnumeric.

edition-consulted.switches: the function name exists at the edition (IntroducedIn 85 for MAX/MIN/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN)
only the cited rule in the class-agreement diagnostic (EditionInfo; §1989:A.2.x.3 at 85); the check itself is the same
native vs standard-decimal arithmetic arm (num.StandardDecimal); COBOL-85 has no ARITHMETIC clause so it always takes the native arm, the same arm a 2023 program without ARITHMETIC takes

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicRenderer.cs, IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs, IntrinsicCatalog.cs and Runtime/Intrinsics for Edition|CobolVersion|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry; the runtime selection kernel and its ISelectionOrder carriers consult no edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf40_06 covers algebraic value and space extension; the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, alphabetic/alphanumeric mixing and group operands are not exercised

COBOL1627 ORD-MIN argument-2 class alphanumeric cannot agree (§1989:A.2.33.3)

reader.notes: The binder routes a list of nonnumeric (or class-neutral plus nonnumeric) arguments to OrdMinString and sets the collate flag when a PCS is in effect, so CollatePrefix passes __COLLATE; numeric lists compare by value without alignment (ScaledOrder/CobolNum.Compare) or as exact values. Probes agree with the program's own IF relation under the same PCS.
